description.en-US:
The vendor offering this price. Required, because a price with no vendor answers no question worth asking: what makes this a vendor price rather than a cost is precisely that somebody is offering it.

Immutable. Moving a price to another vendor would rewrite what a supplier was recorded as having offered, and any purchase order that resolved through it would keep a price its vendor never quoted.

A plain ulid with no edge — the party belongs to Contacts, and a foreign key across a module boundary would make Purchase's schema depend on Contacts' table. Validated through a port, which also checks the party actually has a vendor profile.

The product being quoted. The template rather than the variant, because a vendor usually quotes one price for a product line and it would be tedious to repeat it per colour.

Always set, even when product_variant_id narrows the quote to one variant. That is what lets resolution find every candidate for a product in one read and then prefer the variant-specific one, rather than issuing two queries and merging them.

The single variant this price is for, or NULL for a price covering the whole template.

Nullability IS the specificity mechanism: a variant-specific price beats a template-wide one from the same vendor (PRICE-INV-018), so leaving it NULL is how a vendor's general quote is expressed rather than a missing value. It must belong to the template above, which the domain service checks — a variant from a different product would make the two columns describe different things.

The unit the vendor quotes in, which need not be the unit stock is counted in: a supplier sells by the carton while the warehouse counts bottles.

Required, because a price without its unit is not a price — 220,000 per carton and 220,000 per bottle are entirely different offers. It must share a UoM category with the product's inventory unit (BR-PRICE-UOM-003), checked through Essential's conversion port; otherwise the converted quantity would be a number in the wrong dimension.

The currency the vendor quotes in (BR-PRICE-CUR-002). Required and singular: an imported product may be quoted in USD while the books are kept in VND, and an amount whose currency is only assumed is the failure BR-PRICE-CUR-004 names.

There is no FX service, so this is carried and compared, never converted. A purchase order in another currency is the caller's problem to reconcile — and knowing that it must is exactly why the currency is recorded here.

The smallest quantity this price applies from, in purchase_uom_id. Quantity breaks are separate rows rather than a nested structure, so a vendor offering 1+ at 250 and 100+ at 220 is two ordinary records.

Required with a default of zero rather than nullable: resolution compares against it on every candidate, and a NULL would have to be treated as zero anyway — at which point the column may as well say so.

What the vendor charges per unit of purchase_uom_id, in currency_id.

This is NOT the product's cost and must never be copied onto it (PRICE-INV-009, BR-PRICE-VARIANT-009). A vendor's offer and what the business has actually paid and valued are different numbers, routinely different in practice: a product costing 10,200 may be offered at 10,000 by one vendor and 9,500 by another. Cost is Inventory's to calculate from goods actually received.

Zero is permitted. A free sample still has a price to be recorded at, and forbidding zero would push those through some other mechanism where they do not belong.

When this price starts applying, or NULL for always. Effective dating rather than editing in place: a price rise announced for next quarter must not change what is being ordered today, and the superseded price is still needed to explain the orders placed under it.

When it stops applying, or NULL for open-ended. Exclusive of the instant itself, matching every other window in this module, so one price ending and the next beginning at the same moment leaves no gap and no overlap.

Closing a window is the preferred way to record a new commercial term (section 24): set valid_to on the old row and create a new one, rather than overwriting a price the business genuinely offered at the time.

How long this vendor takes to deliver at this price. It belongs on the price rather than on the vendor because the two travel together: a cheaper bulk price frequently carries a longer lead time, and that trade-off is the whole content of the quote.

Zero means same-day rather than unknown. Bounded at ten years because a longer figure is a data-entry error, not a supply chain.

Breaks ties between rows that are equally specific and equally applicable, lowest winning (section 27 step 6). It does NOT override specificity or quantity: a variant price beats a template price whatever their sequences, or a low sequence on a general quote would silently undo every specific one.

With id as the final tie-break, this is what makes purchase price resolution deterministic (PRICE-INV-020) — two otherwise indistinguishable rows still resolve the same way on every run, which is what makes the outcome testable.

What the vendor calls this product in their own catalogue. Carried so an order, an enquiry or a dispute can quote the reference the vendor will recognise, rather than an id that means nothing at their end.
The vendor's own name for the product, which is often not the buyer's. Kept for the same reason as the code: the words on the vendor's invoice should be findable from here.
